Utilities & C Compatibility

On this page

Hardware Abstraction Layer (std::hal) ​

std/hal/ wraps common embedded peripherals as methods on a struct instance holding the peripheral's MMIO base address — construct one with its static new() (GpioPin::new(...), Uart::new(...)), then call methods on it. Each driver is generic over a chip type that knows that peripheral's registers, picked at compile time from the variable's type (the same pattern as BST<K, V, C>'s ordering) and checked against a chip trait, so the calls compile down to direct register accesses. Every module is freestanding-safe (no libc dependency) and works with plain --target cross-compilation as well as --freestanding.

c
#include <std/hal/gpio.h>
#include <std/hal/uart.h>

void blink(&volatile unsigned int gpioa, &volatile unsigned int usart2) {
    struct GpioPin<Stm32F4Gpio> led = std::GpioPin::new(gpioa, 5, GPIO_OUTPUT);
    led.write(1);
    led.toggle();
    struct Uart<Stm32F4Usart> con = std::Uart::new(usart2, 115200u, 42000000u);
    con.write_str("blink\n");
}

Peripheral base addresses are &volatile unsigned int references, so every register access is a volatile load or store. Make one from a datasheet address once, inside unsafe — the compiler can't know the address is valid:

c
&volatile unsigned int GPIOA_BASE() {
    unsafe { return (&volatile unsigned int)0x40020000UL; }
}

Remember that struct types aren't namespaced even though their static methods are called through the namespace — struct GpioPin, but std::GpioPin::new(...) from outside namespace std (see Namespaces). The chip type comes from the declared variable, so new takes no type argument.

Drivers and Chips ​

ModuleHeaderTypeDescription
GPIOhal/gpio.hGpioPin<C>GpioPin::new(base, pin, direction); set_direction, write, read, toggle, set_pull
I2Chal/i2c.hI2cBus<C>I2cBus::new(base, speed, clock_hz); write, read, write_read (write, then read), probe; a failed transfer still sends STOP, releasing the bus
SPIhal/spi.hSpiDevice<C>SpiDevice::new(base, mode); transfer (one byte, full-duplex), cs_assert/cs_deassert, write(tx, ?&rx, len) (rx may be null), read
UARThal/uart.hUart<C>Uart::new(base, baud, clock_hz); write_byte, read_byte, write_str, rx_ready, tx_ready
Timerhal/timer.hTimer<C>Timer::new(base, prescaler); set_period, start, stop, read, clear_flag, flag_set
Watchdoghal/watchdog.hWatchdog<C>Watchdog::new(base, timeout); enable (typically cannot be disabled once armed), feed, caused_reset

Constants: GPIO_INPUT/GPIO_OUTPUT, GPIO_PULL_NONE/GPIO_PULL_UP/GPIO_PULL_DOWN; I2C results I2C_OK/I2C_NACK/I2C_ERROR; SPI_MODE_0–SPI_MODE_3 (CPOL/CPHA = 00, 01, 10, 11).

clock_hz is the peripheral's input clock, used to compute the baud-rate or bus-speed divider; Uart::new with clock_hz = 0 keeps the rate the boot firmware set.

Chip Types ​

Chip typePeripheral
GpioGeneric, UartGeneric, SpiGeneric, I2cGeneric, TimerGeneric, WatchdogGenericThe reference register layouts below — for an FPGA soft core or a simulator that implements them
Pl011ARM PrimeCell PL011 UART (QEMU virt, Raspberry Pi, many Arm SoCs)
Ns1655016550-compatible UART with byte-wide registers at consecutive addresses (QEMU RISC-V virt, many SoCs)
Stm32F4GpioSTM32 GPIO port (MODER/PUPDR/IDR/ODR/BSRR; the F2/F4/F7/L4/G0/H7 layout). write uses BSRR, so it needs no read-modify-write
Stm32F4UsartSTM32F1/F2/F4 USART (SR/DR/BRR/CR1)
Stm32F4SpiSTM32F1/F2/F4 SPI as master, software NSS, fPCLK/16. Chip select is an ordinary GPIO there: cs_assert/cs_deassert do nothing — drive a GpioPin
Stm32F4I2cSTM32F1/F2/F4 I2C ("v1": CR1/CR2/DR/SR1/SR2/CCR/TRISE), standard and fast mode
Stm32F4TimSTM32 general-purpose timer (TIM2–TIM5): PSC, ARR, CNT, update flag UIF. The counter runs at clock / (prescaler + 1)
Stm32F4IwdgSTM32 independent watchdog: timeout is the 12-bit reload value counted at LSI / 256 (about 8 ms per unit at 32 kHz); caused_reset reads RCC_CSR.IWDGRSTF at the STM32F4 RCC address

A chip type is a struct whose methods take the peripheral's base address and do the register work, as the matching chip trait lists them, so another part is supported by writing one more such struct.

The Pl011, Ns16550, Stm32F4Usart, Stm32F4Tim and Stm32F4Spi chips run against QEMU's models of those peripherals in tests/stdlib/baremetal/qemu/run.sh, and every chip's register sequence is checked against RAM-backed registers in the hosted tests.

Chip Traits ​

Each driver's chip parameter is bounded by a trait that lists the register operations the driver calls. Every method takes the peripheral's base address as an unsigned long and is const: a chip type holds no state of its own (the std chips have a single unused int field).

TraitRequiresBoundsSatisfied by
GpioChipset_direction(base, pin, direction), write(base, pin, value), read(base, pin), toggle(base, pin), set_pull(base, pin, pull)GpioPin<C: GpioChip>GpioGeneric, Stm32F4Gpio
UartChipinit(base, baud, clock_hz), tx_ready(base), rx_ready(base), put(base, c), get(base)Uart<C: UartChip>UartGeneric, Pl011, Ns16550, Stm32F4Usart
I2cChipinit(base, speed, clock_hz), write(base, addr, data, len), read(base, addr, data, len), probe(base, addr) (the I2C_* results)I2cBus<C: I2cChip>I2cGeneric, Stm32F4I2c
SpiChipinit(base, mode), transfer(base, tx), cs(base, asserted)SpiDevice<C: SpiChip>SpiGeneric, Stm32F4Spi
TimerChipinit(base, prescaler), set_period(base, period), run(base, on), count(base), flag(base), clear_flag(base)Timer<C: TimerChip>TimerGeneric, Stm32F4Tim
WatchdogChipinit(base, timeout), enable(base), feed(base), caused_reset(base)Watchdog<C: WatchdogChip>WatchdogGeneric, Stm32F4Iwdg

Naming a driver with a chip that lacks one of the methods is an error at the declaration, not deep inside the driver:

text
struct Uart<Stm32F4Gpio> con = Uart::new(base, 115200u, 0u);
error: type 'Stm32F4Gpio' does not satisfy constraint 'UartChip' for generic
       parameter 'C' of struct 'Uart' (no method 'init')

A part of your own conforms by having the methods; nothing is declared against the trait. Code written over the trait works for every chip:

c
#include <std/hal/uart.h>

// A debug port with one write-only data register at base + 0.
struct DebugPort {
    int           unused_;
    void          init(unsigned long base, unsigned int baud, unsigned int clock_hz) const;
    int           tx_ready(unsigned long base) const;
    int           rx_ready(unsigned long base) const;
    void          put(unsigned long base, unsigned char c) const;
    unsigned char get(unsigned long base) const;
};
void DebugPort::init(unsigned long base, unsigned int baud, unsigned int clock_hz) const { }
int  DebugPort::tx_ready(unsigned long base) const { return 1; }
int  DebugPort::rx_ready(unsigned long base) const { return 0; }
void DebugPort::put(unsigned long base, unsigned char c) const {
    unsafe { *(&volatile unsigned int)base = (unsigned int)c; }
}
unsigned char DebugPort::get(unsigned long base) const { return (unsigned char)0; }

// Written once, for every UART chip.
generic<C: UartChip>
void banner(&Uart<C> con) {
    con.write_str("boot\n");
}

int main() {
    unsigned int reg = 0u;
    struct Uart<DebugPort> con = Uart::new(&reg, 0u, 0u);
    banner(&con);
    return reg == 10u ? 0 : 1;   // the last byte written was '\n'
}

Reference Layouts ​

The *Generic chips use these registers (byte offsets from base, 32-bit registers, one bit per pin for GPIO):

ChipRegisters
GpioGenericDIR +0x00 (1 = output), OUT +0x04, IN +0x08, PULL_EN +0x0C, PULL_SEL +0x10 (1 = up, 0 = down)
UartGenericDATA +0x00, STATUS +0x04 (bit 0 RX ready, bit 1 TX ready), BAUD +0x08 (written with baud)
SpiGenericDATA +0x00, STATUS +0x04 (bit 0 busy, bit 1 TX ready), CTRL +0x08 (mode | 0x80 enable), CS +0x0C (0 = asserted)
I2cGenericDATA +0x00, STATUS +0x04 (bit 0 busy, bit 1 ACK, bit 2 error), CTRL +0x08 (1 START, 2 STOP, 4 SEND, 8 READ+ACK, 16 READ+NACK), ADDR +0x0C, SPEED +0x10
TimerGenericCTRL +0x00 (bit 0 enable), PRESCALER +0x04, PERIOD +0x08, COUNT +0x0C, STATUS +0x10 (bit 0 flag)
WatchdogGenericCTRL +0x00 (bit 0 enable), TIMEOUT +0x04, FEED +0x08 (write 0x6969), STATUS +0x0C (bit 0: last reset was a watchdog reset)

All are polling-based drivers (no interrupt-driven variants) operating directly on raw MMIO addresses — see std::interrupt for the interrupt-handling side (ISR registration, vector tables, MMIO bitfield helpers) if a peripheral needs to signal completion asynchronously instead.

ARM Cortex-M ​

hal/cortex_m.h — NVIC, SysTick, SCB as global instances at their standard Cortex-M memory-mapped addresses; see Bare-Metal → ARM Cortex-M for the full walkthrough (HAL usage, DSP-extension intrinsics, MVE).

c
#define NVIC_BASE     0xE000E100UL
#define SYSTICK_BASE  0xE000E010UL
#define SCB_BASE      0xE000ED00UL

struct Nvic {                      // global instance: nvic (nvic_init())
    &volatile unsigned int base;
    void  enable(unsigned int irq);
    void  disable(unsigned int irq);
    int   is_pending(unsigned int irq) const;
    void  clear_pending(unsigned int irq);
    void  set_priority(unsigned int irq, unsigned char priority);
    unsigned char get_priority(unsigned int irq) const;
};

struct SysTick {                   // global instance: systick (systick_init())
    &volatile unsigned int base;
    void  start(unsigned int reload, int use_core_clock);
    void  stop();
    unsigned int read() const;
    int   flag_set() const;        // COUNTFLAG: wrapped since last read
};

struct Scb {                       // global instance: scb (scb_init())
    &volatile unsigned int base;
    void  system_reset();
    void  enable_fault(unsigned int fault_mask);   // SCB_FAULT_* bits
    void  disable_fault(unsigned int fault_mask);
    void  set_vtor(unsigned int addr);             // relocate the vector table
    int   in_handler_mode() const;                 // 1 inside an exception handler
    void  set_psp(unsigned int addr);              // process stack pointer
    void  set_msp(unsigned int addr);              // main stack pointer
};

#define SCB_FAULT_USAGE  (1u << 18)
#define SCB_FAULT_BUS    (1u << 17)
#define SCB_FAULT_MEM    (1u << 16)

AArch64 ​

hal/aarch64.h — targets ARMv8-A application cores (Cortex-A53/A57/A72/ A55/A76), distinct from the Cortex-M microcontroller HAL above.

System registers (free functions, no instance needed): aa64_read_mpidr() (processor affinity/CPU ID), aa64_read_currentel() (exception level EL0–EL3), aa64_read_daif()/aa64_write_daif() (interrupt mask bits), aa64_irq_enable()/aa64_irq_disable(), aa64_fiq_enable()/aa64_fiq_disable(), aa64_isb()/aa64_dsb_sy()/ aa64_dmb_sy() (barriers).

Generic Timer (Aa64Timer, global instance aa64_timer): read_cntpct() (system counter), read_cntfrq() (counter frequency), set_tval(), enable()/disable(), fire_pending().

GIC (GICv2-compatible; GicDist/GicCpu, global instances gic_dist/gic_cpu, initialized via gic_init(dist_base, cpu_base); default bases GIC_DIST_BASE = 0x08000000 and GIC_CPU_BASE = 0x08010000, the QEMU virt / Juno layout): enable_group0, enable_irq/disable_irq, set_priority, set_target (CPU affinity mask), set_config (edge- vs level-triggered), is_pending/clear_pending on the distributor; ack() (returns the pending IRQ number), eoi() (end-of-interrupt) and running_priority() on the CPU interface.

RISC-V ​

hal/riscv.h — addresses follow the SiFive FE310 / standard RISC-V MMIO map.

CSR access (free functions, backed by inline asm): rv_csr_read_mstatus/rv_csr_write_mstatus, rv_csr_read_mie/ rv_csr_write_mie, rv_csr_read_mip, rv_csr_read_mcause, rv_csr_read_mepc/rv_csr_write_mepc, rv_csr_read_mtvec/ rv_csr_write_mtvec, rv_csr_read_time/rv_csr_read_cycle/ rv_csr_read_instret, plus rv_global_irq_enable/rv_global_irq_disable.

CLINT (Clint, global instance clint, via clint_init(base); default base CLINT_BASE = 0x02000000): set_msip/clear_msip (per-hart software interrupt), set_mtimecmp/ read_mtime, schedule(delta) (timer interrupt delta ticks out).

PLIC (Plic, global instance plic, via plic_init(base); default base PLIC_BASE = 0x0C000000, IRQs up to PLIC_MAX_IRQ = 53): set_priority, enable/disable, set_threshold, claim() (highest- priority pending IRQ, 0 = none), complete(irq).
